et øjekast.explanation: "Et øjekast" means "a glance". It is built from "et øje" (an eye) and "et kast" (a throw), so it is a throw of the eyes. To say how something seems at first glance, use "ved første øjekast" (at first glance): "Ved første øjekast er det en god pris" (At first glance it is a good price).

et øjenbryn.explanation: "Et øjenbryn" means "an eyebrow". To say someone raises an eyebrow, use the verb "at løfte" (to lift): "Han løftede et øjenbryn" (He raised an eyebrow).

et øjenlåg.explanation: "Et øjenlåg" means "an eyelid". It is built from "et øje" (an eye) and "et låg" (a lid). In other words, "et låg" is also a lid on a pot: "et låg på en gryde" (a lid on a pot).

et økosystem.explanation: "Et økosystem" means "an ecosystem". It is built from "øko" (eco) and "et system" (a system). The same "øko" is in "økologisk" (organic): "økologiske æg" (organic eggs).

et ønske.explanation: "Et ønske" means "a wish". To say a wish came true, use "gå i opfyldelse" (to come true): "Mit ønske gik i opfyldelse" (My wish came true). The verb is "at ønske" (to wish): "Jeg ønsker dig held og lykke" (I wish you good luck).

et øre.explanation: "Et øre" means "an ear". It is also a small unit of money worth a hundredth of a krone. To say a price with it: "Mælken koster tre kroner og halvtreds øre" (The milk costs three kroner and fifty øre).

øde.explanation: "Øde" means "deserted". For a place that is just calm and peaceful, use "stille" (quiet) instead: "Byen er stille" (The town is quiet).

ødelagt.explanation: "Ødelagt" means "broken". It comes from the verb "at ødelægge" (to destroy). To say a day or a plan is ruined: "Dagen er ødelagt" (The day is ruined).

ødelæggelse.explanation: "Ødelæggelse" means "destruction". It comes from the verb "at ødelægge" (to destroy). To talk about the damage after a flood: "Oversvømmelsen efterlod store ødelæggelser" (The flood left great destruction).

ødelæggende.explanation: "Ødelæggende" means "destructive". It comes from the verb "at ødelægge" (to destroy). To describe a fire that does great damage: "en ødelæggende brand" (a destructive fire).

øjeblikkelig.explanation: "Øjeblikkelig" means "immediate". It is built from "et øjeblik" (a moment). To ask for help right away, use it before the noun: "øjeblikkelig hjælp" (immediate help). To say how someone acted, use "øjeblikkeligt" (immediately) after the verb: "Han svarede øjeblikkeligt" (He answered immediately).

øjeblikkeligt.explanation: "Øjeblikkeligt" means "immediately". To say how quickly a person acts, use it after the verb: "Han svarede øjeblikkeligt" (He answered immediately). Before a noun, use "øjeblikkelig" (immediate): "øjeblikkelig hjælp" (immediate help).

øjensynligt.explanation: "Øjensynligt" means "apparently". It contains "øje" (eye) and "syn" (sight). It can also come first in the sentence: "Øjensynligt er han træt" (Apparently he is tired).

økologisk.explanation: "Økologisk" means "organic". In Denmark, organic food in shops carries the red "Ø-mærket" (the organic mark). To talk about organic eggs, use the plural ending: "økologiske æg" (organic eggs).

økonomisk.explanation: "Økonomisk" means "economic". When you describe a car that costs little to run, it means "economical": "en økonomisk bil" (an economical car).

øm.explanation: "Øm" means "sore". To say a body part is sore when touched: "Min arm er øm" (My arm is sore). To say something hurts, use "at have ondt" (to hurt): "Jeg har ondt i armen" (My arm hurts).

ønskelig.explanation: "Ønskelig" means "desirable". It comes from the verb "at ønske" (to wish). To say it would be good if everyone comes: "Det er ønskeligt, at alle kommer" (It is desirable that everyone comes).

øreringe.explanation: "Øreringe" means "earring". It is the plural, used when you mean more than one: "Jeg køber to øreringe" (I am buying two earrings).

øst.explanation: "Øst" means "east". To name the eastern part of a region, put it before the name: "Østjylland" (eastern Jutland).

østersøen.explanation: "Østersøen" means "the Baltic Sea". The Danish island Bornholm lies in it: "Bornholm ligger i Østersøen" (Bornholm lies in the Baltic Sea).

østpå.explanation: "Østpå" means "east". It is built from "øst" (east) and "på" (on). To say where a place lies, use "øst for" (east of) instead: "København ligger øst for Roskilde" (Copenhagen is east of Roskilde).

øvelse gør mester.explanation: "Øvelse gør mester" means "Practice makes perfect". Literally, it says that exercise makes a "mester" (master).

øverst.explanation: "Øverst" means "at the top". The opposite is "nederst" (at the bottom): "Navnet står nederst på siden" (The name is at the bottom of the page).

en / et.explanation: "En / et" means "a". Each Danish word takes only one of them: "en bil" (a car) but "et hus" (a house). To stress the number one, add an accent: "Jeg har én bil" (I have one car).

at padle.explanation: "At padle" means "to paddle". The tool you paddle with is "en pagaj" (a paddle): "Jeg har glemt min pagaj" (I have forgotten my paddle). For rowing with oars, use "at ro" (to row) instead: "Vi roer over søen" (We row across the lake).
